generator.params.note: Flora of China (vol. 23, p. 150), Caryota mitis (read 2026-10-18): clustered stems to 10 m and 8 to 20 cm through; petioles 0.8 to 2 m; the rachis 2 to 2.8 m with 9 to 23 primary pinnae a side, each with 10 to 20 secondary pinnae a side. Drawn as stems 0.06 m in radius; fronds 3.6 m long, the petiole 0.3 of them (about 1.1 m); the pinnae from the family's rule (sixteen pairs, fifteen leaflets a side), the longest pinna 0.18 of the frond (0.65 m) and its longest leaflet a third of the pinna (0.2 m, within the 7 to 25 cm PROSEA gives, read 2026-10-18); five fronds a year living three years, full size within a few years of a stem's start, the stem rising 0.12 m a year besides, each 2.5 cm up the stem from the last; four suckers from the fourth year, most within a few years of it (estimated, set by eye from photographs).

traits.clonal.note: Flora of China (vol. 23, p. 150), Caryota mitis: stems clustered; Flora of North America (vol. 22): clustered, 15 cm through or less.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A clump's usual height, about 7 m, set below Flora of China's 10 m greatest.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of China (vol. 23, p. 150), Caryota mitis: stems to 10 m.

traits.stem_diameter_max_m.note: Flora of North America (vol. 22), Caryota mitis: stems 15 cm through or less; Flora of China (vol. 23, p. 150) gives 8 to 20 cm.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of China (vol. 23, p. 150), Caryota mitis: the rachis 2 to 2.8 m.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of China (vol. 23, p. 150), Caryota mitis: petioles 0.8 to 2 m.

traits.pinnae.note: Flora of China (vol. 23, p. 150), Caryota mitis: 9 to 23 primary pinnae on each side of the rachis.

traits.leaflets.note: Flora of China (vol. 23, p. 150), Caryota mitis: 10 to 20 secondary pinnae on each side of a primary one, with one at its tip.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 4 m at 10 years and 7 m at 20 to the top of the crown, under Flora of China's 10 m stems. Wide tolerances.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy: a clustered fishtail palm with twice-pinnate fronds of wedge-shaped, jagged leaflets. Each stem is hapaxanthic, flowering from the top down and then dying while the clump lives on, which is not drawn.
